Title: LSJ Undue Influence and no repeat

Messages.Author: wedge
Messages.Body:
Count Zaroff has an Enrage on. He Enrage rushes, Amaranths and goes to
the uncontrolled region.
On the following turn, Undue Influence(qui) is played on him.

Does he recognize that it is a different turn? Or does he think it is
the same turn since he was out of play.

If he sees that it is a different turn does Enrage burn imediantly?

Matt

Messages.Author: Meej
Messages.Body:


I think generally a minion newly becoming controlled recognizes a new
turn, but that Enrage and other cards which say "this turn" or "your
next discard phase" or whatever, and are in play, are always checking
for you to reach an end-of-turn, at which point they will burn. One
of the other links I found while looking talked about contesting a
Chain-of-Command vampire and a Spell-of-Life mummy-vampire, and how if
the CoC vamp ends up winning, when it comes back it's passed the point
at which CoC would have shuffled it in (CoC no longer being in play),
and gets to hang around. This has always seemed like a contradiction
to me, but LSJ's been consistent about how he's ruled on them.

My guess is that for any effect (Zaroff, Lay Low, Descent into
Darkness, Banishment) that takes a vampire and its cards out of play,
and any cards that would burn "at the end of this turn" or some other
particular moment in time, they'll always check for that once they
come back into play. But as long as Zaroff got chances to keep being
Undue Influenced into play, using that rush, and eating people in
order to go back into hiding, he and his rage would be safe. Once he
hung around to the end of a turn, the Enrage would burn.

Seems expensive, though, what with the 1 pool, though I suppose you
could make that pay for itself by taking one back off of him (so that
his being full after all the snacking didn't put him right back in
play).

- D.J.

The apparent inconsistency, which you've definitely made clear enough

Examples:
Khabar: Glory on a banished vampire - burns on any of your untap
phases if in play, per above-linked ruling.
Enrage on Count Z etc - burns at the end of any turn if in play.
Chain-of-Command'ed vampire that contested - is apparently a strange
edge case, as an effect based on a card that doesn't stay in play.

Question:
Vampire A equips with a Baseball Bat/Leather Jacket, and is then
Banished during the same turn, before the Bat can untap xer. On a
later turn, xe is returned to play via Undue Influence, and taps to
perform an action of some sort. Does xe untap at the end of that
turn, as there's a lingering, unfulfilled effect from the Baseball
Bat? Or is that somehow different than the "burn myself" effect that,
using the same wording for timing, Enrage sets up? And if so, how/
why? (Designer Intent is a legitimate answer, of course, but it's not
clear from card text alone.)

There are many effects based on cards that don't stay in play.
Torn Signpost is a favorite, due to historical rulings.
The Leandro tax is another.

> Question:
> Vampire A equips with a Baseball Bat/Leather Jacket, and is then
> Banished during the same turn, before the Bat can untap xer. On a
> later turn, xe is returned to play via Undue Influence, and taps to
> perform an action of some sort. Does xe untap at the end of that
> turn, as there's a lingering, unfulfilled effect from the Baseball
> Bat? Or is that somehow different than the "burn myself" effect that,
> using the same wording for timing, Enrage sets up? And if so, how/
> why? (Designer Intent is a legitimate answer, of course, but it's not
> clear from card text alone.)

Successfully equipping (via an action) a Leather Jacket produces two effects: it
places the Leather Jacket on the acting minion and it sets up a "untap the
acting minion" effect to be triggered at the end of the turn.

That effect will be applied at the end of the turn even if the minion loses the
Leather Jacket (burning it for damage prevention, for example). The effect is
not one based on the card being in play (the minion would untap at the end of
every turn in that case).

So, if the minion is not in play when the effect is triggered (e.g, xe's been
Banished), then the effect will not untap xer when it goes off (just as CoC's
effect wouldn't move xer to the bottom of the crypt with the rest).

It differs from the Enrage case in that Enrage's "burn me" effect is an effect
of the card (Enrage) being in play.

Messages.Author: witness1
Messages.Body:


By default, effects generated by cards in play are continuous while
the card is in play. Leather Jacket's effect isn't continuous, and so
requires conditional text to indicate this.

Cards that aren't put into play _can't_ have continuous effects while
in play, so no such text is needed to indicate that they don't.

-witness1

Messages.Body:

>
>> Leather Jacket's effect is worded with the conditional clause (the trigger), so
>> that distinguishes it from Enrage.
>
> Ah. So it takes a conditional clause to separate the effects, then?

Not exactly. It just takes being written as something other than an effect
generated by the card being in play.

For instance, that could be accomplished just by listing the effect before the
"put me in play" effect of a card.

For instance, having a Melange on you doesn't give you +1 intercept.

And simply having a Blood Brother Ambush in play does not prevent all combats
from ever occurring.

See also Dark Influences, Dual Form (the original vampire's capacity doesn't get
restored if xe goes to torpor), Acceptance PA cards, Life Boon, Minor Boon,
Monomancy, Not to Be, etc.

> And again, how is this meant to have been evident other than by
> ruling?

Context.
